articles.title: Film Company Wants to Hypnotize People So They Can Watch Classic Movies for the First Time Again
articles.summary: French film production and distribution company Pathé is performing an experiment to see if it can wipe classic movies from people’s minds and let them experience them afresh.
body: Pathé is working in collaboration with hypnotist Victor Kraemer to mind wipe 30 movie buffs to see if they can relive that first viewing. The event is called Pathé Rewind.

Just before the film screening, participants will once again be put under hypnosis by Victor Kraemer, after which the selected film will be shown on the big screen. Three movies are being considered — The Matrix, Se7en, La La Land and Interstellar — and one will be chosen based on which has the most familiarity to the chosen 30.
What’s in the box? Are we living in a simulation? What happens when you go really far away? Can Ryan Gosling sing? Imagine not knowing the answers to these questions.

Pathé said there is no guarantee any of this will work, of course, but it’ll be interesting to see the outcome. From a distance. I don’t want to be memory wiped, thank you. Especially when you consider the following disclaimer: “Pathé accepts no liability for the outcome, the effect, or any other consequences of the hypnosis sessions.
points: French film production and distribution company Pathé is performing an experiment to see if it can wipe classic movies from people’s minds and let them experience them afresh.

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Sells 4 Million Copies in 72 Hours
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero is officially the next big thing. Developer S-Game has announced that its wuxia-themed action game has surpassed a significant milestone in just a few days. Within 72 hours of going on sale, Phantom Blade Zero has sold 4 million copies.
body: Even on its first day, it was clear this was going to be a beast. Phantom Blade Zero was ahead of Steam’s biggest games, from PUBG to Dota 2, topping the Steam charts as soon as it launched. It was also the best-selling game on Steam by revenue, ahead of Modern Warfare 4, Aion 2, and Probably Stolen, a Cyberpunk shopkeeper sim that's going viral. Steam concurrents peaked on Sunday with a whopping 833,921 players.

The early success shouldn't come as a huge surprise. Last week, it was estimated that Phantom Blade Zero had sold over 1 million copies before launch across launch platforms Steam and PS5, and Tencent’s WeGame (an online PC storefront in China). Nearly two thirds of total prelaunch sales were from China, Taiwan, or Hong Kong.
IGN's Phantom Blade Zero review returned a 9/10. We said: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger."
Phantom Blade Zero is a monster hit, but it's not quite on par with Black Myth: Wukong, which managed 10 million sales in the first three days.
points: Phantom Blade Zero is officially the next big thing.

articles.title: Yakuza Creator's Studio Officially Shuts Down After Backers Desert It
articles.summary: Nagoshi Studio, the developer founded by Yakuza creator Toshihiro Nagoshi, has officially closed its doors after backer NetEase stopped its funding. Nagoshi Studio had been working on Gang of Dragon, a Yakuza-style crime drama starring Ma Dong-seok.
body: Japan's official gazette, Kanpo, confirmed that the company was dissolved on Oct. 31. Back in March, Bloomberg reported that NetEase had decided to cut off Nagoshi Studio after learning that Gang of Dragon would cost another 7 billion yen ($44 million) to complete. Nagoshi Studio reportedly failed to find another backer for the game.

Gang of Dragon was revealed at the 2025 Game Awards with a cinematic trailer that suggested an even more realistic and more violent take on gangster life in Tokyo's Kabukicho district than that presented in the Yakuza games.

Chinese giant NetEase has been slimming down its gaming portfolio and divesting overseas investments since 2024, closing multiple studios as a result. Among these was a new MMO studio from World of Warcraft designer Greg Street.

Nagoshi Studio was founded in 2022 by Nagoshi and key members of Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio, the Sega team responsible for the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series. Nagoshi had been at Sega for over 30 years, where he worked on Daytona USA, Shenmue, and Super Monkey Ball before creating the Yakuza series.

articles.title: Dead by Daylight Devs Apologize After TheBurntPeanut Stream Stirs Controversy in Its Community
articles.summary: Behaviour Interactive has responded after what appeared to be a Dead by Daylight collaboration with controversial streamer TheBurntPeanut caused backlash in its community.
body: Halloween weekend may have been more eventful for the team behind the hit multiplayer horror game than they may have expected. What started as a relatively contained negative reaction has since exploded into a full-blown breaking point for players, with some reporting that they've uninstalled Dead by Daylight after seeing its developers work with TheBurntPeanut.

The Canadian studio was first put on the hook by the more vocal members in its community when they discovered the streamer, who gained popularity over the last year for playing extraction shooters like Arc Raiders, was dipping his toes into the horror multiplayer game for the first time. The Halloween season was bound to result in a small uptick in attention for Dead by Daylight, but for those who have stuck by it through its 10 years of service, the jump scare arrived when the streamer revealed he had been gifted access to its entire rogues' gallery of Survivors and Killers.
"Wow! Wow!" TheBurntPeanut said while scrolling through dozens of instant unlocks during his Halloween stream. "Guys! I just got all the guys!"

articles.title: Yakuza Series Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down Before Releasing a Game
articles.summary: Gematsu reported that the Tokyo-based Nagoshi Studio closed its doors via a shareholders’ resolution on October 31. The announcement was made in today’s Japanese government gazette Kanpo.
body: Yakuza series creator Toshiro Nagoshi’s studio has officially shut down before it had the chance to release a game.

The Yakuza-like Gang of Dragon was meant to be the debut game from Nagoshi Studio, which Nagoshi formed in 2022 with investment from Chinese megacorp NetEase after he departed Ryu Ga Gotoku a year earlier. But doubt was cast on its future in March when NetEase signalled its intention to cut off funding as part of a broader retreat from international video game investment.

According to Bloomberg, NetEase made the decision to cut Nagoshi’s funding after it learned Gang of Dragon needed at least another ¥7 billion (approx. $44.4 million) to be completed. Nagoshi was apparently trying to find new investors to help buy the studio out, without much luck.
The studio closes nearly a year after Gang of Dragon enjoyed a flashy reveal at The Game Awards in December. Now, it looks like it may never see the light of day.

articles.title: Elon Musk Officially Confirms He Doesn't Get Star Wars
articles.summary: Elon Musk, owner of Tesla and SpaceX, and an avid Grok advocate, has never been shy about expressing his opinion online. He had plenty to say about award-winning director Christopher Nolan's wildly successful adaptation of The Odyssey — including claiming an AI-influenced reimagining of the series…
body: More often than not, these opinions criticize something that isn't there or deliberately misunderstand the story’s point. It's not that Musk can’t have or share these thoughts; they just don't seem grounded in reality. Musk has recently turned his attention to yet another franchise he seems to fundamentally misunderstand: Star Wars.

In a Nov. 1 post on X, Musk shared an AI-generated image of Anakin Skywalker, Padmé Amidala, and Luke and Leia as children, all dressed in black. Anakin, fresh from his bad-boy era in Revenge of the Sith, sits on a spiky throne, with the Emperor’s Royal Guards standing behind him. The characters also appear to be in some kind of hangar — which, if you ask us, isn’t the best place for a throne. But we digress.

The caption reads: “This is what they stole from us.” This refers to the “This is what they took from us” right-wing nostalgia memes, which kicked off in the early 2020s in response to social media posts lamenting the older, arguably more conservative days. As with all things on the internet, the meme has evolved over time, with people online using it to level more tongue-in-cheek criticism towards creators and franchises.
points: Elon Musk, owner of Tesla and SpaceX, and an avid Grok advocate, has never been shy about expressing his opinion online.

articles.title: Soulframe to launch into free open beta this week, as Warframe devs go head-to-head with WoW: Forever
articles.summary: Soulframe's Preludes (its own version of a beta) is finally opening its doors to the whole world ahead of the Verse of the Veilands update. Starting this week, anyone who wants to can simply download the game and hop in, no invite required.
body: The date this happens is an interesting one: 6th November. That's two days after the release of World of Warcraft: Forever and the same week as Old School RuneScape 's Hardcore worlds, so it's suddenly become a pretty packed month for MMO enthusiasts.

This comes after three years of closed testing for the fantasy action MMORPG, which players have been able to gradually see firsthand through sporadic invites. With Soulframe suffering delays since its first reveal, brief invite events have already occurred over this period. Even locked away, the game has received multiple substantial updates over the years, including new quests, Pacts (classes), factions and so on.

As for what newcomers to Soulframe can look forward to when Soulframe opens its doors, the Verse of the Veillands update is bringing a total overhaul of the map progression system this month. After the completion of an early quest, players are introduced to a corrupted landscape, the Veillands, which they must purify.

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Became One of 2026's Best-Selling Games in Just 72 Hours
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero had an incredible opening weekend. It received very positive reviews, reaching a score of 88 on Metacritic, climbed to the top of the charts on Steam, and sold 4 million copies worldwide within 72 hours.
body: Beijing-based studio S-Game released Phantom Blade Zero, a wuxia RPG with soulslike elements, on Oct. 29. Although some players found the combat less challenging than they would've hoped, the fighting sequences are one-of-a-kind, with great animation for each kung fu move and beautiful cinematics. As Paulo Kawanishi put it in Polygon's review of Phantom Blade Zero, it "perfectly captures the meaning of martial arts by chasing more the artistic aspect of the fighting styles and visual poetry of the fantastical battles staged in Wuxia movies."

Estimates indicate the game sold at least one million copies pre-launch. The Chinese gaming market is huge, and all eyes were on Phantom Blade Zero this weekend, especially after its rave reviews, but no one anticipated just how many players would flock to it. It reached 833,000 concurrent players within hours of launch, making it the second-highest-played single-player game of the year after Palworld.

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, selling over 4 million copies in three days
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero studio S-Game has announced that its debut title has sold more than 4m copies in its first 72 hours on sale. The game's official X account broke the news alongside a celebratory message, though without providing a per-platform breakdown of copies sold.
body: "Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!" the developer wrote on X.

Phantom Blade Zero is available on Steam and PlayStation 5, but the 4m figure also includes sales made on the China-exclusive Tencent WeGame PC launcher. Prior to launch, Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott estimated Phantom Blade Zero to have sold over 1m copies before it had even released.
It was always clear the third-person character action game was going to be a hit, we just had to wait for actual figures to be released.

Phantom Blade Zero attracted over 431,000 concurrent players on Steam at launch, a figure that kept risking and rising into the weekend, ultimately settling at a massive 833,921 peak concurrent (via SteamDB ). Just in case it wasn't already clear, this is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, beating the likes of Forza Horizon 6 and far outpacing all other major releases such as Onimusha: Way of the Sword, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Ace Combat 8.

articles.title: As if the injury descriptions weren't already ghastly enough in Dwarf Fortress, the legendary outpost builder is getting a "meat biome"
articles.summary: Legendary outpost builder Dwarf Fortress is getting a meat biome. A terrible netherworld of bone and artery. A sunken redoubt of gristle and gizzard. An appalling labyrinth of squirt and squelch. Honestly, the biggest shock here is that Dwarf Fortress doesn't appear to have a meat biome already.
body: These foul omens arrive care of a massive "Future of the Fortress" thread on the Bay 12 forums, in which studio co-founder (and prominent genAI disliker ) Tarn "Toady One" Adams fields questions about the on-going development. As a forum thread, it's not a formal news source, so please season these tales of gutsy geology with whatever Condiment of Scepticism you consider appropriate.

There's no date for when the new biome might arrive, but Adams says it'll likely exist underground, and will be revolting. "Lots of meat terrain - muscle, bone, vertebral walls, sinew, sphincters," he promised. "We would have rivers of blood/fluids if we ever get to the fluid update, but no new fluids as it stands. We had thrown out the idea for maple syrup style taps on the vertebral walls for cosmic spinal fluid but alas, this is not in the game." At the very least, there won't be any meat trees, but you can mine the meat for resources.
points: Legendary outpost builder Dwarf Fortress is getting a meat biome.

articles.title: The HeroQuest board game is coming to Steam with a quest editor and multiplayer
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: Avalon Hill's deluxe rerelease of the classic dungeon crawl board game HeroQuest is getting a digital edition courtesy of Nomad Games, who previously adapted board games like Talisman, Love Letter, and Fury of Dracula. Expect goblin-bashing, trap-disarming, treasure-hunting, and spell-casting. I'll use my broadsword.

The most promising detail revealed so far is the inclusion of a quest editor so players can create their own maps and missions, as well as downloading quests made by others through mod.io integration.

Hopefully it includes the rules additions from HeroQuest First Light, especially the option to just move eight squares per turn instead of rolling to move if there aren't any monsters on the board. Slogging across the dungeon to get back to the exit 2d6 squares at a time is a real chore otherwise.
HeroQuest: Digital Edition is scheduled for release on Steam in 2027, with a closed beta playtest coming soon.

articles.title: Footage of what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: Persona tragics have been begging for remakes of the first two games in the series for ages (at least, the ones who aren't begging for remakes of the PS2-era Shin Megami Tensei games instead). After thoroughly milking Persona 4 and 5, series producer Kazuhisa Wada said in August, "personally, I think it's something we should definitely do."

Now, almost two minutes of footage from what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked via the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit. It shows some dungeon exploration, typically flashy combat, and a dialogue scene all in the modern Persona style.

Oddly, Tatsuya from Persona 2 is one of the party members, though it's possible this is a cross-promotional skin you can equip. Or maybe the remakes will incorporate some kind of Persona Q-style crossover?

While it's fair to be suspicious this could be AI-generated footage, it seems both a bit too long and too internally consistent for that to be the case. And it's not like Atlus hasn't got form, given that we found out the Persona 3 remake was real via a leak as well.

articles.title: Obsidian's Josh Sawyer on RPG cities: 'Compared to a dungeon, generally speaking, a town is 4x the expense per square foot'
articles.summary: In a new Q&A vlog on his YouTube channel, Obsidian studio design director Josh Sawyer took a question about why there are so few RPGs in contemporary urban settings. Part of the problem, according to Sawyer: They're more difficult and costly to make than other RPG environments.
body: Elsewhere in this section, Sawyer cited Baldur's Gate 2's Athkatla, Disco Elysium, and the recent Zero Parades as RPGs that land the plane on believable, dense urban environments⁠—though Sawyer notes that the latter two have the advantage of not needing to work in as many believable combat encounters as other RPGs.

A few others spring to mind for me: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3's version of the titular city. But all of those really highlight Sawyer's point about expense and challenge. Vampire and Cyberpunk were notoriously difficult development cycles for their respective studios. I'll always be a BG3 Act 3 defender, but it's definitely the part of the game with the most noticeable seams.

But even if they're hard to make, I love urban adventures in RPGs, whether as part or the whole of a game. Novigrad and Oxenfurt are two of my favorite parts of The Witcher 3, for example. For a real niche example of an urban RPG you should have on your radar, I highly recommend the early access Moves of the Diamond Hand.

videos.title: 'Silent Hill: Townfall' - Review
videos.summary: Bold, stark, innovative and uncompromising, 'Silent Hill: Townfall' is full of brilliant elements that feel authentic to the franchise without ever being constrained by it, but a terminally limited core gameplay loop will be the fulcrum on which your enjoyment hinges.
